title: RCS Business Messaging: What It Is, $0.0128 a Text on Twilio
desc: RCS business messaging sends branded texts and rich cards. On Twilio US, an RCS text costs $0.0128 to $0.0145 with carrier fees; a rich card $0.029 to $0.0355.

faqs: How much does RCS business messaging cost?

On Twilio's US price list for November 2026, an RCS text costs $0.0083 per segment plus a carrier fee of $0.0045 to $0.0062, so $0.0128 to $0.0145. A rich media message, such as a card with an image and buttons, costs $0.022 plus $0.007 to $0.0125, so $0.029 to $0.0355, billed once regardless of size. US carrier onboarding fees, and annual and submission fees for brand verification, come on top.

Not for short texts. On Twilio's US list the RCS text price and the SMS price are both $0.0083 per segment, but RCS carrier fees are higher at AT&T and T-Mobile, the two networks we could compare: to AT&T an RCS text costs $0.0128 against $0.0118 for SMS. A long message can be cheaper as one rich card ($0.032 to AT&T) than as three text segments ($0.0384).

Yes, from iOS 18, if the user's carrier supports RCS on iPhone. Apple's support page says RCS messages appear in green bubbles, and users can turn RCS business messages off in Settings, Apps, Messages, RCS Messaging.
What happens if the phone cannot receive RCS?

With Twilio, a Messaging Service that holds both your RCS sender and a phone number sends the message as SMS or MMS instead. Twilio says not all phone numbers can receive RCS messages, so keep an SMS number in the service.
How long does RCS approval take?

Twilio tells you to allow four to six weeks, or longer for several regions. Your brand is verified, then Google, the carriers or both approve the launch; approval times vary by carrier, and you can send to a carrier's users as soon as that carrier approves.
Is a segment in RCS the same as in SMS?

Google's US billing FAQ defines an RCS text segment as 160 bytes of UTF-8 encoded text. In UTF-8, plain English letters take one byte each, so about 160 characters; emoji and many accented letters take several bytes. Rich media messages are not split into segments.
body:
Short answer. RCS business messaging is a richer, branded form of business texting that enhances SMS and MMS: a business sends texts, images, rich cards and buttons from a sender profile that shows its name and logo instead of a phone number. On Twilio's US price list for November 2026, an RCS text costs $0.0083 per segment plus a carrier fee of $0.0045 to $0.0062, so $0.0128 to $0.0145 in total, against $0.0118 to $0.0128 for a plain SMS from a local number.

A rich media message, such as a card with a picture and buttons, is billed as one flat message: $0.022 plus a carrier fee of $0.007 to $0.0135, so $0.029 to $0.0355. That is close to what an MMS costs. If your CRM or white label GoHighLevel SaaS sends through Twilio, RCS sits on the same Twilio price list as your SMS, and a Twilio Messaging Service can fall back to SMS or MMS when the phone or the carrier cannot receive RCS.

This guide explains what RCS business messaging is, who can receive it, how it is billed, what 10,000 messages cost, and how a business gets approved. Prices come from Twilio's US SMS and RCS pricing page, billing rules from Google's RCS for Business US billing FAQ, read on November 24, 2026.

What RCS business messaging is

RCS stands for Rich Communication Services. Twilio describes it as "a modern messaging protocol that enhances traditional SMS and MMS by enabling branded, interactive messages." Google calls its platform RCS for Business; its documentation and web addresses also use RCS Business Messaging, or RBM.

The biggest practical difference from SMS is the sender. According to Twilio's RCS documentation, RCS business messaging "uses a branded sender profile rather than a traditional phone number to send messages." The person sees your display name and logo instead of a 10 digit number, with a banner on Android and your brand color. Google says brands can "build trust with a 'Verified' icon".

What a business can put in a message, per Twilio's documentation:

  • Images, video, audio and files up to 100 MB.
  • Up to 11 suggested replies, and up to 11 suggested actions: open a web page, dial a number, open a map, share a location, create a calendar event or launch an app.
  • Rich cards (text, media and buttons in one message) and carousels of several cards.
  • Typing indicators, delivery receipts and read receipts.

RCS vs SMS for business

FeatureSMSRCS business messaging
Sender shownPhone numberBrand name, logo, verified badge
MediaNone (MMS for pictures)Images, video, audio, files up to 100 MB
ButtonsNo (standard SMS)Up to 11 suggested replies and 11 actions
Read receiptsNo (standard SMS)Yes
Who can receiveAny phone that receives textsAndroid and iPhone on iOS 18, where the carrier supports it
Twilio US price, text$0.0083 per segment + carrier fee$0.0083 per segment + carrier fee
Twilio US price, mediaMMS $0.022 + carrier feeRich media $0.022 + carrier fee

Twilio's list price is the same for an RCS text and an SMS ($0.0083) and the same for a rich media message and an MMS ($0.022). The difference in your bill comes from the carrier fees, which are a little higher for RCS at AT&T and T-Mobile, the two networks where we could compare both.

What RCS costs per message in the US

Twilio bills two kinds of RCS message. In its words, "RCS Rich text messages are charged per segment and RCS Rich Media is charged per message." On top of Twilio's own price comes a carrier fee that depends on the recipient's network. These are the outbound prices on Twilio's US page, current as of November 2026:

Recipient carrierRCS text (Twilio + carrier)RCS rich media (Twilio + carrier)SMS, local number (Twilio + carrier)
AT&T$0.0083 + $0.0045 = $0.0128$0.022 + $0.01 = $0.032$0.0083 + $0.0035 = $0.0118
T-Mobile$0.0083 + $0.0062 = $0.0145$0.022 + $0.0125 = $0.0345$0.0083 + $0.0045 = $0.0128
Verizon$0.0083 + $0.005 = $0.0133$0.022 + $0.007 = $0.029not used here
US Cellular$0.0083 + $0.0062 = $0.0145$0.022 + $0.0135 = $0.0355not used here
All other carriers$0.0083 + $0.0045 = $0.0128$0.022 + $0.01 = $0.032not used here

Three more charges to know about. Inbound RCS also costs money: $0.0083 for a rich text and $0.0165 for a rich media message, plus inbound carrier fees ($0 at Verizon). A message that ends in a "Failed" status costs $0.001. And, as the page says, "RCS senders launching on US carriers are subject to carrier onboarding fees". Twilio's onboarding guide adds that a US sender also pays annual and submission fees to the companies that verify the brand and submit the registration; Twilio does not charge them. The amounts of both are shown only inside the Twilio Console, so we could not read them.

Prices from other providers differ. Telnyx, for example, says its RCS uses "usage-based pricing with no platform fees", but its messaging price page did not show a per message RCS price when we checked.

How RCS billing works: segments, media and sessions

Google tracks the billable events and carriers decide the price. Its US billing FAQ says: "Billable simply means that an event is eligible for a charge. Carriers determine whether and how billable events are charged." The rules that shape your bill:

  • A text is billed per segment. One segment "is equal to 160 bytes of UTF-8 encoded text". In UTF-8, plain English letters take one byte each, so about 160 characters; emoji and many accented letters take more bytes, so fewer characters fit. We assume Twilio counts RCS segments as Google defines them.
  • Rich media is one flat charge. A rich card, a carousel or a file attachment is "billable as a single, flat-rate event, regardless of content size".
  • Button taps can count. "Each tap on a suggested action generates one billable event."
  • You pick a billing category when you create the sender. A non conversational agent is billed for each message it delivers. A conversational agent can be billed a flat rate per 24 hour session, which in the US starts when the business and the user exchange 4 rich or rich media messages, with at least one from the business and at least two replies from the user. The category "can't be changed later" without going through Google's live agent update process.

Outside the US, Google uses a standard billing model with the same two categories: non conversational agents, for which Google lists one time passcodes, alerts and promotional offers as examples, are "billed per message" and conversational agents a flat rate for conversations covering 24 hours. Twilio's US page lists per message prices; ask your provider how it prices sessions before you choose the conversational category.

Worked cost: 10,000 messages to AT&T customers

A hypothetical example using Twilio's November 2026 list prices for recipients on AT&T, before onboarding fees and failed message fees:

What you sendCost per message10,000 messages
SMS, one segment, local number$0.0118$118.00
RCS text, one segment$0.0128$128.00
MMS, local number$0.031$310.00
RCS rich card$0.032$320.00
SMS, three segments$0.0354$354.00
RCS text, three segments$0.0384$384.00

Two things follow from the arithmetic. A short RCS text costs about $10 more per 10,000 than the same SMS to AT&T numbers. And a long message is cheaper as one rich card ($0.032, flat) than as three text segments ($0.0384), so if your reminders run past 320 bytes, a card with a button may cost less than plain text, before any billable taps on its buttons. Note that SMS counts segments differently from RCS, so the same text can split into a different number of segments on each channel.

Who can receive RCS messages

Twilio says RCS "is compatible with Android and iOS 18 devices." Apple's support page adds the conditions on the iPhone side: "To use RCS, you need iOS 18 and a cellular plan from a carrier that supports RCS messaging on iPhone." It also calls RCS "a carrier-provided service" and says "Availability varies by region and carrier."

Three limits to plan around:

  • Not every number can receive RCS. Twilio says "Not all phone numbers can receive RCS messages", and that Messaging Services "send messages using SMS or MMS when RCS messages fail or carriers don't support them." You need a phone number for that fallback.
  • Users can switch business messages off. On an iPhone, Settings, Apps, Messages, RCS Messaging has a separate switch for RCS business messages, and users can report a message as junk.
  • Your sender reaches only approved networks. Google says an approved agent can "reach RBM-capable users on the approved carrier networks."

How to start sending RCS business messages

Twilio's onboarding guide tells you to "allow four to six weeks or longer if you plan to launch in multiple regions." The steps:

  1. Create the sender profile. Display name, description, a 224 x 224 pixel logo (50 kB at most), a 1440 x 448 pixel banner, brand color, contact details, privacy policy and terms URLs. Twilio notes that carriers "typically don't approve RCS Senders with the same display name and logo".
  2. Test it. Add your own phones as test devices and send test messages before approval.
  3. Register with Google. An authorized representative, your opt-in and opt-out descriptions, a screenshot or page that shows the opt-in, a use case description and a short video of the sender in action.
  4. Register for the US. Legal business name as on your IRS EIN letter, EIN, address, website traffic, expected RCS volume, a campaign description, and HELP and STOP sample replies, plus an acknowledgement of the CTIA messaging guidelines.
  5. Wait for carriers. "Approval timelines vary by carrier." Once one carrier approves in a country, you can send to that carrier's users.

Google's launch guide explains why this takes time: some launches are approved by Google on a carrier's behalf and others by the carrier itself, a Google managed carrier needs a launch on at least one carrier managed network in the same country first, and "Certain carriers will reject your launch if they have no contract in place with you". If you already went through 10DLC registration for SMS, much of the business information will be familiar.

Consent rules still apply

In the US, RCS registration still asks how people opt in, what your opt-out message says and what your STOP reply says, and Twilio's guide tells you to set up Advanced Opt-Out handling for the RCS sender. For the wording of an opt-in, see our guide to SMS opt-in language, and for US law on marketing texts, how the TCPA applies to text messages. This is general information, not legal advice.

How RCS compares with WhatsApp and toll free SMS

RCS is one of several branded channels. For WhatsApp's per message prices, see WhatsApp Business API pricing. If you mainly need a trusted number for SMS, compare what a toll free number costs. On Twilio, the RCS sender and an SMS number sit in the same Messaging Service, so a message goes as RCS where it can and as SMS or MMS where it cannot.

If you plan to use RCS buttons and replies to run a chat flow, for booking or order updates, our guide to what an AI chatbot for business costs covers the cost of the bot behind the messages.

What we could not verify

  • The amount of the US RCS onboarding fees (brand verification and submission): Twilio shows them only inside its Console.
  • Per message RCS prices at Telnyx and other providers.
  • A list of which US carriers currently accept RCS business messages, and the approval time of each.
